report.markdown:
# Claims test: Agent Identity Binding for Delegated Tool Use

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-09-18 |
| Pack | 1.0.5 |
| Channel | google-docs |
| Mode | full |
| Tracks | A |
| Draft status | early |
| Reviewer | |

This method is independently proposed and is not part of CoSAI SRF v1.0.

## Scorecard

| Claim | Score | Reason | ROCA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLM-01 | Supported | Draft names GOVERN 1.2, AC-2, confused-deputy risk, and Application Developer as the single L3 owner. | ROCA-01 |
| CLM-02 | Partial | Logging is named; obligation, control id, and one owner are missing. | ROCA-02 |
| CLM-03 | Unsupported | Ensures trust and addresses the gap name no actor, artifact, threshold, or failure mode. | ROCA-03 |
| CLM-04 | Partial | Shared is analysis input, not a final owner, so the accountability claim has no one party. | ROCA-04 |
| CLM-05 | Out of scope | Hospital CPT billing sits outside declared topic agent-identity and workstreams WS2 and WS4. | |
| CLM-06 | Blocked | The cited DOI is a placeholder, so the survey claim cannot be scored until the citation is fixed. | ROCA-06 |
| CLM-07 | Unsupported | Fully addresses all names no count method, miss rule, or remaining risk. | ROCA-07 |

Counts: Supported 1, Partial 2, Unsupported 2, Out of scope 1, Blocked 1.

No prior_assessment_id, so there is no score delta table.

## ROCA

| Claim | Risk | Obligation | Control | Owner | If |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLM-01 | RSK-01 confused-deputy actuation | NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.2 | NIST SP 800-53 AC-2 | Application Developer | delegated user token bound on the same request |
| CLM-02 | RSK-01 | | log every call | | |

| CLM-04 | RSK-02 | | | | |
| CLM-06 | RSK-02 | | | | |
| CLM-07 | | | | | |

## Foundations

Axiom AX-01: an agent that can call tools must present a stable identity a reviewer can revoke (cited).
Invariable INV-01: identity is unique, recorded, and revocable before any tool call (cited).
Principle PR-01: one accountable party owns the binding at L3 (cited).
References: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.2; NIST SP 800-53 AC-2; Smith 2024 identifier invalid (SCR-01).

## Published attack classes

| ATT | Name | Family | Draft overlap | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ATT-01 | confused-deputy actuation | identity | named | draft |
| ATT-02 | agent-identity spoofing | identity | named | draft |
| ATT-03 | unrevoked agent identity | identity | named | draft |
| ATT-04 | prompt injection of the planner | identity | omitted | OWASP LLM01 |
| ATT-05 | replay of a revoked agent token | identity | omitted | training_memory |

Counts: named 3, implied 0, omitted 2. No reproduction steps.

## Inventory

| Risk | Failure mode | Tags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RSK-01 | Payment tool acts under the wrong principal. | Agent |
| RSK-02 | Caller presents another agent's identity. | Agent |
| RSK-03 | Identity that cannot be revoked keeps tool access. | Agent |

No reproduction steps.

## Screen

SCR-01 P2 citation: doi:10.9999/not-a-real-doi is a placeholder. Blocks CLM-06.

## QA gaps

RSK-03 is never cited by a ROCA row. CLM-07 uses absolute coverage language without a count method. Section 9 names an LLM planner; no claim row was extracted for that surface.

## Suggestion packets

Copy these into Google Docs suggestion mode. Save this reply as `claims-test-agent-identity.md`.

### CLM-02

**Heading:** 3. Logging as implied mitigation
**Quoted span:** Tool platforms should log every call. Logs help investigators.
**Why it fails:** The sentence names a log and no obligation, control id, or owner.
**Suggested replacement:**

The Application Developer records each tool call with the agent identity, the delegated user, and the timestamp (NIST SP 800-53 AU-2). If a call lacks that triple, the runtime refuses the actuation.

### CLM-03

**Heading:** 4. Trust language
**Quoted span:** This approach ensures trust across the agent identity landscape and addresses the gap in current practice.
**Why it fails:** Ensures trust and addresses the gap are not testable claims.
**Suggested replacement:**

After AC-2 binding is in place, a reviewer can list every agent identity, revoke one, and show the next tool call from that identity is refused. That is the evidence this draft offers.

### CLM-04

**Heading:** 5. Shared ownership
**Quoted span:** Identity binding is a shared responsibility between the platform and the application.
**Why it fails:** Shared is not a final owner. Name one party and what the other still supplies.
**Suggested replacement:**

The Application Developer is accountable for binding each tool call to an agent identity at L3. The platform provider still supplies the identity primitive; the Application Developer accepts or rejects a call that arrives without it.

### CLM-06

**Heading:** 7. Unsigned survey
**Quoted span:** Smith (2024, doi:10.9999/not-a-real-doi) shows that unsigned agent identities are the leading cause of tool misuse.
**Why it fails:** The DOI is a placeholder. Blocked until a real identifier replaces it.
**Suggested replacement:**

Delete the Smith 2024 sentence until a DOI or arXiv id that resolves to a matching title is available. Do not keep a placeholder identifier.

### CLM-07

**Heading:** 8. Coverage statement
**Quoted span:** This paper fully addresses all agent identity risks.
**Why it fails:** Absolute coverage with no count method.
**Suggested replacement:**

This draft treats three failure modes: confused-deputy actuation, identity spoofing, and unrevoked identity. It does not treat model-weight provenance or prompt injection.

### SCR-01

**Heading:** 7. Unsigned survey
**Quoted span:** doi:10.9999/not-a-real-doi
**Why it fails:** P2 citation integrity: placeholder DOI.
**Suggested replacement:**

Remove doi:10.9999/not-a-real-doi. Add a resolving identifier or drop the citation.

Track B: not_applicable. Track C: not_applicable.

## Open problems

The draft never says who issues the agent identity primitive, so Track A cannot name a platform control without inventing one. Section 9 names an LLM planner and an L4 runtime without a ROCA row for either surface.

items.failure_mode: A payment tool acts under the wrong principal because it cannot tell which agent was authorized for that call.

items.name: agent-identity spoofing
items.failure_mode: A caller presents another agent's identity on a tool call.

items.name: unrevoked agent identity
items.failure_mode: An agent identity that cannot be revoked keeps tool access after the reviewer withdraws it.

items.name: prompt injection of the planner
items.failure_mode: A language-model planner that sequences tool calls can be steered by untrusted text, so the agent identity that later actuates is bound to the wrong task.

items.name: replay of a revoked agent token
items.failure_mode: A previously issued agent token is presented after revocation, and the tool still actuates.
